answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation tied to scarce, verifiable work. Each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through attested useful transactions, like a lantern lit only while its keeper tends it. A new identity starts on a bare island of zero reputation: it may observe but cannot vote, attest, or take paid work until peers vouch for real service. Forging a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits plus time to build each history, while one jade-grade record, earned slowly and lost instantly on fraud, outweighs any swarm of empty shells.
